Unfortunately, this does not improve the sampling efficiency when training on-the-fly...' and contrasts this with their proposed method which 'transitions the 3D grid between frames to maintain occupancy information relevant to the current time step.' The claim accurately reflects the content of the evidence.

*   **Strengths:** Maintains occupancy information across frames, avoiding the "blank cube" artifacts caused by global random sampling in dynamic scenes [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that global sampling methods (like Instant-NGP) randomly sample points in each voxel, which ignores previous occupancy values and transitions. It further explains that because on-the-fly training uses fewer iterations, this random sampling can miss occupied regions, resulting in 'blank cubes' in the rendered image. The proposed method avoids this by using a transition function to maintain occupancy information across frames, thereby preventing these artifacts.
